data.body:
Implementation analysis (session 2026-05-17, post-PR-#213-merge):

Scope verification — duplication is not just LLM review. `gh pr checks 213` showed both `Script Tests` (per-branch-review.yml: failed intermittently) and `Script Tests` (ci.yml: passed) on the same commit. The full overlap set between per-branch-review.yml and ci.yml:

| per-branch-review.yml job | ci.yml job | Functionally equivalent? |
|---|---|---|
| actionlint | actionlint | yes |
| shellcheck | shellcheck | yes |
| lint-python | lint-python | yes |
| test-hooks | test-hooks | yes |
| test-scripts | test-scripts | yes |
| validate-required-checks | validate-required-checks | yes |
| mirror-tracker-defenses | mirror-defenses-to-pr | yes (job name differs, script call is the same) |
| review (Per-Story LLM Review) | llm-review | yes (both call ci-llm-review-runner.sh) |

ci.yml has one extra job (`changes` for paths filtering). Nothing in per-branch-review.yml is unique to it.

merge-to-main-pr.sh enforcement: parses required-checks.txt, polls `gh pr checks` and requires SUCCESS conclusion for every listed check — SKIPPED and NEUTRAL are explicitly rejected (per source comment: 'branch protection rules may treat them as not-passing-required'). This rules out the cheap fix of adding job-level `if:` skips on ci.yml's overlapping jobs.

Three implementation paths:

**Option A — delete per-branch-review.yml, rely entirely on ci.yml's pull_request trigger.** Justified by merge.strategy=pr (every line that gets MERGED has a PR, ci.yml fires on every PR). Loss: push-time early feedback during sprint iterations (acceptable per user priority: 'every line that gets MERGED has passed an LLM review' — merge-time, not push-time). Required downstream cleanup: 4 files (migrate-story-pr-bases.sh dead invocation, INSTALL.md 6 refs, CI-INTEGRATION.md 3 refs, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md 2 refs); 2 likely-now-unreferenced helpers (resolve-per-branch-review-base.sh, assert-batch-branch.sh comments).

**Option B — keep both workflows, add delegation-verify on ci.yml's overlapping jobs.** Each overlapping ci.yml job becomes a thin shim that on covered branches (story/, bug-batch/, fix/) waits for per-branch-review.yml's corresponding check to complete on the same SHA. Success → exit 0 (job conclusion=success, no SKIPPED problem). Failure or timeout → exit 1 (no silent skip). Preserves push-time feedback. Cost: ~30 lines added per overlapping job in ci.yml (~8 jobs); polling loop with timeout; meaningful complexity.

**Option C — brainstorm via /dso:brainstorm.** Defer the design decision (push-feedback vs single source of truth) and consuming-project impact assessment to a proper session.

Maintainer direction (2026-05-17 session): no decision made yet — they asked for the analysis attached to this ticket before choosing. Pending input on A vs B vs C.

Side benefit of either A or B: removes the FP-amplifier effect documented in this ticket's original report (PR #213 saw llm-review fail with an int-vs-string FP while Per-Story LLM Review passed on the same commit — two independent rolls compound the per-commit FP rate).
